title: Longitudinal microbiome shifts after coastal flooding

manuscript.abstract: We study microbiome shifts after coastal flooding using repeated household samples. The analysis suggests water intrusion changes bacterial diversity and may affect respiratory outcomes.
manuscript.methods: Households were sampled monthly. DNA sequencing was performed and results were normalized by read depth. The current manuscript clearly shows that flooding changes all exposed communities in a way that is obviously relevant to public health but the text still needs more direct evidence links.
manuscript.results: Observed diversity increased in exposed homes and returned toward baseline after remediation. The estimated effect size was larger in homes with persistent moisture.
manuscript.limitations: The pilot cohort is small and future work should replicate findings across more regions.

claims.text: Flood exposure increases microbial diversity in sampled homes.
Hospital admissions declined after a regional policy intervention.

results.summary: Microbial diversity increased in exposed homes after flooding and moved toward baseline after remediation.
Persistent moisture was associated with a larger estimated effect size.

reproducibilityAttempts.notes: Clean-room rerun reproduced reported diversity trends and stored execution logs.
Earlier attempt predated dependency pinning and did not include all source data.

corpus.title: Microbial exposure after hurricane flooding
corpus.abstract: A pilot study of household microbial exposure after hurricane flooding. Limitations include small sample size and unresolved replication across regions.

corpus.title: Respiratory health after household remediation
corpus.abstract: Remediation studies report mixed respiratory health outcomes and call for future work that links environmental sampling to clinical endpoints.
